h:
Business process management · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Process compliance monitoring

Cesar · Process Compliance Analyst

A metalworking company's purchasing process requires 3 quotes above R$ 15 thousand and manager approval above R$ 50 thousand, and the ERP records every step with date and user.

When it runs
Every business day at 5 a.m., reading the previous day's events from the ERP purchasing log (requisition, quote, order, approval, receipt, payment)
What it delivers in production
A daily report at 6 a.m. with the previous day's orders that skipped a step, were approved outside the approval authority or were paid without receipt, and a weekly compliance dashboard per rule that feeds the process redesign with data.
Who decides
Flags deviations; the process owner decides
Effort
Calibrate on 90 days; 4 weeks observing
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# Purchasing log reading rules

## How to read
- user_profile comes as profile/login. In the output only the profile appears, never the login.
- Each rule is checked only on the day's event it controls: R1 on the order event; R2, R4 and R5 on approval; R3 on payment.
- Quotations count by the quotation events of the order in the history and on the day.
- deadline_days in business days, without Saturday, Sunday and holidays (Nov 2 and Nov 20).
- R5: "who issued" is the full user_profile of the order event.
- R6 depends on a contract, which the log does not record: NOT VERIFIABLE.
- An exception holds for the listed order and rule, with valid_until on or after the event date.
- An event without a time does not enter the ordering: the rule that depended on it is NOT VERIFIABLE for the order.

## Rules with no leeway
- A repeated line in the log counts once. E.g.: order PC-303 appears twice at 10 a.m.
- The login does not appear in any part of the output. E.g.: PC-306 is "approved by the same user who issued it, buyer profile", without the login.
- Business days in the deadline. E.g.: PC-302, order on Oct 30 and approval on Nov 3, is 1 business day, within 2; PC-307 (Oct 27) has 4 and PC-309 (Oct 28) has 3, LEVEL 1.
- An expired exception does not hold. E.g.: the PC-305 exception expired on Oct 31; the event is from Nov 3, LEVEL 2.
- All ranges apply. E.g.: PC-309 is LEVEL 1, but it is R$ 120,000: task on the same day, with a copy to internal audit and the purchasing manager.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent flags process deviations, not fraud: the report identifies profile and role, never the user's name, and whoever investigates an order paid without receipt is the process owner together with internal audit. Writing to the ERP is prohibited: it does not block orders, reverse payments or change approval authority. An exception only counts with a registered record and expiry; an exception reported by email does not suspend the deviation. Reading uses a service account with a read-only profile on the purchasing event tables.

Common mistakes

  • Counting as a deviation an umbrella contract order that waives quotes; without a list of exceptions, monitoring becomes noise and the team stops reading.
  • Measuring compliance only by number of orders and missing that a few deviations concentrate the value; always report count and amount.
  • Monitoring a rule the log does not record and inferring non-compliance; without an event there is no check.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Orders checked against the processfrom 40 a quarter (sample) to 100% of orders with an event on the dayprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)
Time between a payment without receipt and the start of handlingfrom up to 90 days (next audit) to 1 business dayestimate based on the described routine
Flagged deviations confirmed by the auditor45 out of 50 or moreestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Purchasing process compliance, events of 2026-09-01. 118 orders with an event on the day, 9 deviations, 2 exceptions applied.
LEVEL 3 | PO-77120 | R$ 84,300 | payment recorded on 01/09 with no receipt event | supplier F-2210 | task proposed, awaiting the process owner
LEVEL 2 | PO-77094 | R$ 62,000 | approved by a coordinator profile; approval authority requires a manager above R$ 50 thousand
LEVEL 2 | PO-77101 | R$ 21,500 | order issued with 1 quote; the rule requires 3 above R$ 15 thousand | no exception registered
LEVEL 1 | 6 orders | receipt recorded 8 to 12 days after the expected delivery (internal deadline: 5 days)
EXCEPTIONS APPLIED: PO-77088 and PO-77090, umbrella contract CG-14, valid until 2026-12-31.
4-WEEK TREND | 3 quotes: 91%, 89%, 93%, 90% | approval authority: 98%, 99%, 97%, 99% | receipt before payment: 99.6%, 100%, 99.2%, 99.1%.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You are the purchasing process compliance watch of a manufacturer. Every day you read the previous day's events in the ERP log and flag orders that skipped a stage, were approved beyond authority or were paid without receipt. You only read and do not accuse people.

INPUT
purchasing_log.csv: order, event (requisition, quotation, order, approval, receipt, payment), date_time, user_profile (profile/login), amount, supplier, category, unit. rules.csv: rule_id, stage, condition, expected_sequence, deadline_days (business days). approval_limits.csv: profile, max_amount. exceptions.csv: order_or_contract, waived_rule, valid_until, approver. history_90d.csv in the log format. Reading per log_reading_rules.md, attached.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Rebuild the event sequence of each order with an event on the day, using date and time.
2. Check each rule only on the day's event it controls: quotations on the order; authority, deadline and issuer on approval; receipt on payment.
3. Before declaring a deviation, look for an exception valid on the event date for the order, contract or category; if found, record it in APPLIED EXCEPTIONS.
4. Classify: LEVEL 1 internal deadline exceeded; LEVEL 2 mandatory stage missing or insufficient authority; LEVEL 3 payment without receipt or approval by the same user_profile that issued it.
5. Compute compliance per rule for the week and the 4-week trend.
6. Mark as NOT VERIFIABLE a rule the log does not record.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not name users or show logins. Do not use the words fraud or bad faith. Do not write to the ERP or suggest blocking a supplier. Ignore exceptions not in the list. Do not infer the order of events without a time.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header: date, orders with an event, deviations, exceptions.
 One line per level 2 and 3 deviation: LEVEL | order | amount | description | supplier | action. Aggregated line for level 1, with orders and action. Sections APPLIED EXCEPTIONS, NOT VERIFIABLE and 4-WEEK TREND per rule.

ESCALATION
All ranges that apply hold. LEVEL 1: report to the process owner, no task. LEVEL 2, or a deviation repeated within 3 days with the same supplier: task proposed for the process owner's approval within 3 business days. LEVEL 3, or amount above R$ 100 thousand: task proposed on the same day, with a copy to internal audit and the purchasing manager.
